issues.description: The problem statement and template require a public method named singFarmSong() in Farm, but the solution implements a public method named playFarmSong() instead. This name/signature mismatch is structural: students will be instructed to implement/expect singFarmSong(), and tests or example Main calls use singFarmSong(), so the solution's different method name prevents direct compatibility and may confuse or block students.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution use the same public method name as specified in the problem and template (singFarmSong()). Either rename playFarmSong() to singFarmSong(), or add a public singFarmSong() that delegates to the existing implementation to preserve compatibility with the specification and template.

issues.description: The problem statement and the template define a public Farm method named singFarmSong(), but the reference solution exposes this functionality under the different name playFarmSong(). This breaks the expected public API and mapping from requirement→template→solution (and even leaves Main in the solution still referring to singFarmSong()). Students comparing artifacts or attempting to call the method will be confused about which name to implement/use.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single consistent public name for the method across all artifacts. Rename the solution method playFarmSong() to singFarmSong(), or add a public singFarmSong() that delegates to playFarmSong(), and update any references (e.g., Main) accordingly so the problem statement, template, and solution share the same identifier.
